reason: Ligulate is already ruled to strap-shaped (rule C189); 'narrowly' is a degree modifier that does not change the shape class.

An inflorescence 'a monad' is reduced to a single flower, and pollen in monads is shed as single grains rather than tetrads or polyads; both mean borne singly. The pollen sense is a distinct palynological character that may later deserve its own class beside a tetrad/polyad set.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (bearer hairy PATO_0000454 + trichome PO_0000282 part of the bearer, white)
reason: A compound of two statements: the part is hairy, and its hairs are white. The colour belongs to the trichomes, not to the peduncle or fruit.

target: docs/odp/05-range-with-extremes.md (bearer inflorescence axis PO_0020122, length PATO_0000122)
reason: A measurement of the inflorescence axis, i.e. a bearer plus length with a numeric range; for 'leaf' rows the axis is the rachis.
A calyx or perianth 'enlarging in fruit' is accrescent; 'in fruit' is handled by the stage context and 'not enlarging' by negation.
Misspelling of papillose and the Portuguese papiloso: a surface bearing papillae.

target: new: conjunction of two values (flattened PATO_0002254 and trigonous FLOPO:0991120)
reason: Both values hold at once (a trigonous body flattened on one axis); written unhyphenated, it is not a continuum between two shapes.
Tufted is an exact synonym of caespitose, and its definition already says 'dense tuft'; 'densely' adds no new quality.
Secondary veins that join in a series of loops before reaching the margin are brochidodromous. The quality inheres in the leaf or lamina, not in the vein.
Rhipidium is an exact synonym of the PO class: it is an inflorescence type, i.e. a part, not a quality.

label: infrafoliar
definition: A positional quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of its being borne on the stem below the crown of living leaves, among or below the leaf scars. NOTE: Palm terminology, with interfoliar (among the leaves) and suprafoliar (above them); sibling of FLOPO:0991117 cauline.
reason: A standard palm character with no PATO or FLOPO term; written as a relation to the leaves it would lose the fixed sense of 'below the leaf crown'.
Émergé/emerso leaves and inflorescences of aquatic plants rise above the water. The cactus 'pericarpel emerged' sense (not sunk in the stem) does not fit and should go to review.
'Aril covering the seed entirely' or 'sarcotesta covering half' is a relation to another part, with the extent of covering as the value. It is not a quality of the aril alone.
A part: the blade of the organ described (leaf lamina PO_0020039 when the organ is a leaf). 'Sheaths without laminae' resolves to the bladeless rule (leaf lamina absent).
The definition of sheathing already places the tube at the base of the bearer, so 'basally' is redundant.
Nervation pennée, pinnatinervia and pinnate venation all mean a single primary vein with secondaries on either side.
A hyphenated shape compound is read as a continuum between its two values (playbook, chain_from_phrase).
'Without blotch' negates blotchy (synonym blotched); the position words ('on upper lobe') stay in the record.

label: supramedial
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being located between the midpoint and the margin of the structure that bears it, nearer the margin than the midrib. NOTE: Fern sorus position, between FLOPO:0991299 medial (sensu botany) and FLOPO:0991328 intramarginal.
reason: A standard fern term filling the gap between the existing medial and intramarginal classes. 'Placenta slightly supramedial' uses another sense (above the middle of the ovary) and should go to review.
'Nectaries extrafloral' names the PO class extrafloral nectary; 'present' is then the presence rule.
French discret / Spanish discreto applied to veins and glands means hardly visible, the same as the 'obscure' rule. The occasional 'discrete' (separate) sense does not fit.
Patulous / Latin patulus means spreading, as patent is ruled to spreading (rule C224).
Atropurpureus means dark purple.
'Borne singly' is already an exact synonym of solitary; the bare adverb needs the same rule.
Viny stems or plants grow as vines, i.e. climbing, as lianescent is ruled to climbing (rule C354).

target: new: measurement of a region of the bearer (length PATO_0000122 of the connate portion)
reason: 'Connate for 3 mm' is connate (FLOPO:0991067, pattern 16) plus a length of the fused region. It is not a new quality.

target: new: measurement of a region of the bearer (depth PATO_0001595 of the notch)
reason: A measurement of the apical incision of a notched (PATO_0001495) bearer; 'notch' alone was rejected as a generic part.
Spelling variant of lenticellate (rule C204), also Spanish/Portuguese lenticelado.
Uninervé/uninervis means one-veined, a count of veins like '5-nerved'.
A tissue, not a quality; on stems and branchlets the more specific shoot axis periderm (PO_0005048) applies.
